call_points.text: FY27 EBITDA margin expansion of 50-75 bps over FY26 is reaffirmed, to be delivered quarter by quarter.
Expects double-digit revenue growth and EBITDA ahead of top line in FY27.
Tea costs are roughly flat year on year and benign; India tea margins are where management wants them.
Arabica at $2.99; US coffee margins should climb in about two months as high-cost inventory clears.
Vietnam soluble plant expansion expected online very early in 2027; board has approved a tea extracts capacity expansion.
Sitting on roughly ₹3,000 Cr of net cash.
Packaging and LPG costs have risen; a broad fuel price increase would be the main margin risk.
Middle East shipping disruption hit Capital Foods exports in March; April is back to normal.
India business delivered 16% underlying volume growth in Q4FY26 and 13% for FY26.
Growth businesses crossed ₹4,000 Cr revenue, up 24% in FY26 and 33% in Q4FY26.
Consolidated working capital days improved to 21 in FY26 from 26; India business had negative 2 days.
Innovation-to-sales stood at 4.5% in FY26 with 80 new product launches during the year.
International business grew 11% (CC) in Q4 led by US Coffee; FY26 growth was 9% (CC).
Non-branded business growth accelerated to 41% (CC) in Q4; FY26 growth was 23% (CC).
Capital Foods and Organic India combined grew 8% in Q4, with exports declining 9% owing to geopolitical disruptions.

Double-digit revenue growth with EBITDA ahead of top line
A&P to sales ratio in the 7.5%-8.5% band
Growth businesses to grow about 30% in the near term
Full-year EBITDA margin expansion of 50-70 bps maintained
Growth businesses to grow 30% (aspiration 25-30% for Capital Foods and Organic India)
India tea volume growth mid-single digit
Starbucks top-line growth close to high single digit

industry: Fast Moving Consumer Goods > Agricultural Food & other Products > Tea & Coffee

operating_notes.text: Consolidated net cash (cash and cash equivalents net of total borrowings) was ₹2,978 Cr as of 31 March 2026.
India business working capital was negative 2 days in FY26; consolidated working capital days improved to 21 from 26.
Free cash flow to EBITDA was 107% in FY26 versus 92% in FY20.
Board approved capital investment of up to ₹160 Cr to set up a new 2,000 MT Instant Tea manufacturing facility in India, funded via internal accruals.
Sampann full-year revenue was ₹1,600 Cr, growing 69% in Q4 and 46% for the year.
Vietnam soluble plant is running at 99% utilisation; expansion expected online very early in 2027.
Growth businesses contributed 31% of the India business in FY26 and grew 33% in Q4.
Sampann pulses revenue is ₹600-700 Cr against a ₹2,20,000 Cr pulses market with 6% branded penetration.
Tata Salt share is close to 39% with an ambition to cross 40%; salt MRP for the orange pack moved from ₹30 to ₹32 in June.
Water availability is in about 75% of the country but real distribution and marketing reach is only 40-50%, with north and west largely white space.

timeline.summary: ICRA reaffirmed Tata Consumer Products' [ICRA]AAA (Stable) and [ICRA]A1+ ratings for ₹850 Cr bank facilities and ₹1,500 Cr commercial papers.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹5,433.62 Cr (+17.9% YoY), net profit to shareholders ₹419.08 Cr.
Tata Consumer Products' FY26 investor presentation (8 May 2026) showed consolidated revenue up 15% to ₹20,290 Cr, EBITDA up 12% to ₹2,815 Cr at 13.9% margin, and a recommended ₹10 per share dividend.
Tata Consumer Products approved a capital investment of up to ₹160 Cr to set up a new 2,000 MT Instant Tea manufacturing facility in India.
Tata Consumer Products Limited hosted an analysts/institutional investors call on May 08, 2026, to discuss audited financial results for Q4FY26 and FY26, approved by the Board.

Tata Consumer Products' Q4FY26 earnings call (8 May 2026) reaffirmed FY27 EBITDA margin expansion guidance and double-digit revenue growth; with tea costs benign and US coffee margins expected to recover.
Tata Consumer Products submitted its Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report for FY26.
Q1FY27 call: revenue up 12% to ₹5,349 Cr, EBITDA margin 13.6% (+70 bps YoY), growth businesses at 36% of India mix; FY27 margin guidance of 50-70 bps maintained.
